attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's answer to R7's direct question — is `an f-decided member needs an ablation arm that fails` the right transferable form? No: it is one control kind. The general form is contrastive, and Assurance 2.0 states the same discipline for evidence generally (ask whether the evidence is more likely under the claim than under the counterclaim, so that it discriminates). ADOPTED AND MADE EXECUTABLE: every EC member now declares {proposition, counterclaim, intervention, subject_quantity, asserts} and scripts/emb-battery-control.mjs §3 derives its verdict from them. The specialization is explicit — P = the capability is supported by the declared externalization, N = the declared support is absent, I = support-set ablation, therefore the test must fail under ablation. Three of the ten members name interventions this artifact CANNOT run (authority_mutation, objective_inheritance_mutation, lineage_edge_mutation) and each is declared unmodelled rather than silently skipped: unrunnable is a different verdict from vacuous.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, generalizing ROUND7_MOSAIC_BRIEF.md §2.3. SRC-A20-2024-DEFEATERS for the discriminating-evidence formulation.

readjudicated.method: redeclared_by_target — a declared design invariant is adopted deliberately, not inherited
readjudicated.note: The source-lane status is recorded in imported_from.source_status as provenance. This field records that the TARGET lane re-established it; the two are separate facts and the gate reads this one.

attrs.review_focus: The rule is declared and enforced for ONE intervention kind. The other three have no model here, so TEST-CONTRAST is only mechanically checkable for support_ablation — which is itself an instance of the gap it names.
attrs.statement: A test offered as evidence for a proposition must name the proposition, a relevant counterclaim, and an intervention that distinguishes them, and must satisfy verdict(T|P) != verdict(T|N) under a positive control. R7's ablation rule is the support-dependence specialization of this.
